ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are moving to significantly expand their copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, seeking to add over 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings revealed the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks. The move substantially escalates one of the most significant music copyright cases against generative AI. The case could have major implications for how AI companies are permitted to use commercially released recordings in training data.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement across approximately 30,000 works. The expansion follows a pattern of major record labels broadening their AI litigation as discovery uncovers the scale of training data use. The case is proceeding alongside related actions against other AI music platforms.

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to dismiss Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI company MiniMax's attempt to have Disney's copyright lawsuit dismissed, allowing the case to proceed. Disney and Warner Bros. alleged that MiniMax's AI system was trained on or used to reproduce their copyrighted content without authorisation. The ruling keeps alive one of the prominent entertainment industry cases against generative AI firms.

ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors bringing copyright claims over Meta's Llama AI model have expanded their lawsuit to name Meta's AI scientists individually, not just the company. The move is a notable legal tactic that could expose individual researchers to personal liability for decisions made about AI training data. The case is among several high-profile author actions against major AI developers.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will introduce an AI policy after a nominated anthology was withdrawn amid controversy over AI-generated content. The Stardust anthology's withdrawal spotlighted growing tensions around AI use in comics publishing and awards recognition. The move reflects broader industry pressure on awards bodies to address AI-created works explicitly.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over AI voice replication raises unresolved questions about whether vocal likeness can be protected under existing copyright and IP law.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering new regulations to address AI services that summarise news content without licensing or compensating publishers, a growing concern for the media industry.

ip_further_links.title: Mind the Gap: States Step in to Address Ownership of AI-Generated Works Amid Federal Uncertainty
ip_further_links.summary: With no federal consensus on AI-generated work ownership, individual US states are beginning to introduce their own legislation to fill the gap.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creatives urge the government to 'hold the line' on AI and copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry representatives are calling on the government not to weaken existing copyright protections in response to lobbying from AI companies.

ip_further_links.title: Matt Comyn urges Australia to resolve AI copyright standoff
ip_further_links.summary: CBA chief executive Matt Comyn has publicly urged the Australian government to break the deadlock between AI companies and rights holders over copyright, warning of broader economic consequences.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
ip_further_links.summary: CEPA argues that Europe's existing copyright framework is creating obstacles for AI development, placing EU companies at a competitive disadvantage relative to US and Chinese rivals.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the rise of AI-assisted research is fundamentally changing how academic users interact with scholarly content, and whether publishers are adapting quickly enough.

ip_further_links.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: US media organisations are opposing moves by the federal government to soften copyright protections in ways that would benefit AI developers at the expense of content creators.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis warns that mounting copyright litigation and licensing uncertainty pose a systemic legal risk that could significantly constrain the commercial growth of generative AI.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collecting society SIAE is positioning itself as a key actor in developing frameworks for compensating rights holders whose works are used in AI training.
